source: Durian Orchard (ការដាំធូរេន), by Vann Thana Busab and Montry Vong Phanith, published by the Northwest Cambodia Provinces Fruit Culture Development Committee (Battambang), 1998, 59pp, AIDOC code 178-001
text:
To help prevent fruit-splitting near harvest, the source recommends a foliar/soil application of potassium nitrate (13-05-45) at 150-300 grams dissolved in 20 liters of water, applied only if there has been a run of continuously rainy weather that risks causing the fruit to take up water too fast and split; this should be applied 1-2 times during that risk period, not as a routine schedule.

If growers are top-working or grafting scion wood onto durian rootstock during this period, they should be careful to select disease-free scion material (from a tree with no history of stem canker) and treat the graft union promptly with fungicide paste, since a fresh graft wound is an easy infection point.
